name: 海鮮丼 ゆたか水産 (Kaisendon Yutaka Suisan)

claims.text: Bowls are served with miso soup and seafood/nigiri are eaten with soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce or wheat-free dashi is documented, so wheat exposure should be assumed.

name: 金沢カレー＆ハントンライス だいだい（橙） (Kanazawa Curry & Hunton Rice Daidai)

claims.text: Core dishes use flour-thickened curry roux, panko-breaded fried fish, shrimp and pork cutlet, all fried together; no dedicated fryer or gluten-free handling is documented.

name: 金沢おでん いっぷくや (Kanazawa Oden Ippukuya)

claims.text: All oden items are simmered together in one shared dashi pot, and the broth and many items (fish cakes, the signature wheat-gluten 車麩) contain wheat/gluten, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.

name: 金沢おでんとおばんざい酒場 さんさん (Kanazawa Oden to Obanzai Sakaba Sansan)

claims.text: Kanazawa oden is built on soy-and-dashi broth and includes wheat-based items such as 車麩 (wheel-shaped wheat gluten); fried items like karaage are wheat-battered, so shared broth and fryer cross-contact should be assumed.
The menu centers on oden and obanzai seasoned with soy sauce and dashi, which in Japan are virtually always wheat-containing; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Broths and obanzai are typically made with fish dashi and the menu features karaage, mapo tofu and seafood, so vegetable dishes likely share animal-based broth and preparation surfaces.

name: 金沢近江町市場 みやむら (Kanazawa Omicho Ichiba Miyamura)

claims.text: All signature items are kabayaki glazed with a soy-and-mirin tare, which contains wheat; there is no documented gluten-free preparation.
